84|`price_tier` goes in the top-level `size` field, not the size option (Task 1 §6).
85|A row with `match.status != "ready"` has no line to post; it is waiting on a
86|person, and the preview says what for.
87|
88|CART STAGE
89|----------
90|`app.cart.build(matched)` refreshes the live menu, creates the anonymous source
91|cart, and adds `cart`, `manifest`, and `handoff_url`. It is the only impure stage
92|and therefore runs only after the user presses Build the cart.
93|"""
94|
95|from __future__ import annotations
96|
97|import json
98|import sys
99|
100|# name, module, entry point, description, pure?
101|#
102|# "Pure" means the stage only reads: same run in, same run out, nothing sent
103|# anywhere. Those stages run every time the preview is read, so the page always
104|# shows a match that agrees with the rows as they are right now. The cart stage
105|# is not pure — it creates a real order on the store's server — so it only runs
106|# when somebody presses the button.
107|STAGES = [
108|    ("import", "app.importer", None,
109|     "Normalize collected orders and resolve each row to the store's options", True),
110|    ("match", "app.matcher", "match", "Match each row to a live menu item", True),
111|    ("cart", "app.cart", "build", "Build the cart and produce the handoff link", False),
112|]
113|
114|
115|class PipelineNotReady(RuntimeError):
116|    """A downstream stage has not been built yet."""
117|
118|
119|def _load(module_name: str, attribute: str | None):
120|    try:
121|        module = __import__(module_name, fromlist=["*"])
122|    except ImportError:
123|        return None
124|    if attribute is None:
125|        return module
126|    return getattr(module, attribute, None)
127|
128|
129|def status() -> list[dict]:
130|    """Which stages exist right now. The preview page renders this honestly."""
131|    report = []
132|    for name, module_name, attribute, description, pure in STAGES:
133|        report.append({
134|            "name": name,
135|            "module": module_name,
136|            "description": description,
137|            "pure": pure,
138|            "ready": _load(module_name, attribute) is not None,
139|        })
140|    return report
141|
142|
143|def next_stage() -> dict | None:
144|    for stage in status():
145|        if not stage["ready"]:
146|            return stage
147|    return None
148|
149|
150|def enrich(run: dict) -> dict:
151|    """Run the read-only stages, skipping any that aren't built yet.
152|
153|    Cheap, repeatable and safe to call on every read: it sends nothing anywhere
154|    and re-derives its own output, so a preview built from it can never disagree
155|    with the rows it is showing. Nothing is saved by this — the caller decides.
156|    """
157|    result = dict(run)
158|    for _name, module_name, attribute, _description, pure in STAGES:
159|        if attribute is None or not pure:
160|            continue
161|        entry = _load(module_name, attribute)
162|        if entry is not None:
163|            result = entry(result)
164|    return result
165|
166|
167|def process(run: dict) -> dict:
168|    """Run the saved import through every stage that exists.
169|
170|    Returns the run with whatever downstream stages produced merged in. Raises
171|    PipelineNotReady if the next stage is not built, so callers can show the
172|    import result and say what is missing rather than pretend.
173|    """
174|    result = dict(run)
175|    for name, module_name, attribute, _description, _pure in STAGES:
176|        if attribute is None:
177|            continue
178|        entry = _load(module_name, attribute)
179|        if entry is None:
180|            raise PipelineNotReady(
181|                f"stage '{name}' is not built yet — expected {module_name}.{attribute}()")
182|        result = entry(result)
183|    return result
184|
185|
186|if __name__ == "__main__":  # python3 -m app.pipeline .runs/<id>.json
187|    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
188|        for stage in status():
189|            print(f"[{'x' if stage['ready'] else ' '}] {stage['name']:8} {stage['description']}")
190|        sys.exit(0)
191|    with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as handle:
192|        run_data = json.load(handle)
193|    try:
194|        print(json.dumps(process(run_data), indent=1, default=str))
195|    except PipelineNotReady as exc:
196|        print(f"pipeline stopped: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
197|        sys.exit(2)

1|# Task 6 — In-App Preview & Reconciliation
2|
3|The preview at `/preview/<run_id>` is the checkpoint between import and the
4|external Kung Fu Tea cart. It shows every parsed row, including rows that cannot
5|currently be ordered, alongside the exact menu item and modifiers that the cart
6|builder will use.
7|
8|## Before handoff
9|
10|- The summary keeps separate counts for requested drinks, mapped drinks, ready
11|  rows, and rows needing attention, plus the current estimated subtotal.
12|- Warning, error, unmapped, and dropped-option rows are highlighted. The raw
13|  spreadsheet value remains visible wherever it differs from the resolved menu
14|  value.
15|- **Review & edit** allows changes to name, drink, size, sugar, ice, milk,
16|  toppings, quantity, and notes. Each change is saved and re-run through the
17|  normal resolver and matcher, so counts, prices, warnings, and available option
18|  lists update together.
19|- Saves are serialized, and cart creation waits for the last edit. Clicking the
20|  cart button immediately after leaving a field therefore cannot build from the
21|  stale value.
22|- Unresolved rows do not disappear. The user may fix them in place or continue;
23|  anything that cannot be added is named in the reconciliation.
24|
25|## After cart creation
26|
27|Cart creation opens a distinct third-step view rather than appending another
28|panel below the order. Its single top back control returns to the saved order
29|review; from there the same control returns to import. The cart handoff view
30|includes a reconciliation with:
31|
32|- requested, placed, and not-placed drink counts;
33|- a person-by-person manifest of every confirmed cart line and its modifiers;
34|- every failed or skipped row, its quantity, and the reason;
35|- the live subtotal, tax, fees, and total when Kung Fu Tea returns them; and
36|- store availability and verification warnings.
37|
38|Successful add responses are checked against the final server-side cart
39|read-back. If an acknowledged line is missing, it moves from the placed manifest
40|to the failure list instead of being presented as safe. The user then opens an
41|editable clone on Kung Fu Tea, compares it with this summary, and performs the
42|manual checkout there. Boba Builder never submits payment.

86|def parse_multipart(body: bytes, content_type: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
87|    match = re.search(r'boundary="?([^";]+)"?', content_type or "")
88|    if not match:
89|        return {}
90|    boundary = b"--" + match.group(1).strip().encode()
91|
92|    fields: dict[str, dict] = {}
93|    for chunk in body.split(boundary):
94|        if chunk in (b"", b"--", b"--\r\n", b"\r\n"):
95|            continue
96|        chunk = chunk.lstrip(b"\r\n")
97|        head, _, payload = chunk.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
98|        if not _:
99|            continue
100|        payload = payload[:-2] if payload.endswith(b"\r\n") else payload
101|
102|        headers = head.decode("utf-8", "replace")
103|        name = re.search(r'name="([^"]*)"', headers)
104|        if not name:
105|            continue
106|        filename = re.search(r'filename="([^"]*)"', headers)
107|        fields[name.group(1)] = {
108|            "value": payload,
109|            "filename": filename.group(1) if filename else None,
110|        }
111|    return fields

86|def parse_multipart(body: bytes, content_type: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
87|    match = re.search(r'boundary="?([^";]+)"?', content_type or "")
88|    if not match:
89|        return {}
90|    boundary = b"--" + match.group(1).strip().encode()
91|
92|    fields: dict[str, dict] = {}
93|    for chunk in body.split(boundary):
94|        if chunk in (b"", b"--", b"--\r\n", b"\r\n"):
95|            continue
96|        chunk = chunk.lstrip(b"\r\n")
97|        head, _, payload = chunk.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
98|        if not _:
99|            continue
100|        payload = payload[:-2] if payload.endswith(b"\r\n") else payload
101|
102|        headers = head.decode("utf-8", "replace")
103|        name = re.search(r'name="([^"]*)"', headers)
104|        if not name:
105|            continue
106|        filename = re.search(r'filename="([^"]*)"', headers)
107|        fields[name.group(1)] = {
108|            "value": payload,
109|            "filename": filename.group(1) if filename else None,
110|        }
111|    return fields

1|# Task 6 — In-App Preview & Reconciliation
2|
3|The preview at `/preview/<run_id>` is the checkpoint between import and the
4|external Kung Fu Tea cart. It shows every parsed row, including rows that cannot
5|currently be ordered, alongside the exact menu item and modifiers that the cart
6|builder will use.
7|
8|## Before handoff
9|
10|- The summary keeps separate counts for requested drinks, mapped drinks, ready
11|  rows, and rows needing attention, plus the current estimated subtotal.
12|- Warning, error, unmapped, and dropped-option rows are highlighted. The raw
13|  spreadsheet value remains visible wherever it differs from the resolved menu
14|  value.
15|- **Review & edit** allows changes to name, drink, size, sugar, ice, milk,
16|  toppings, quantity, and notes. Each change is saved and re-run through the
17|  normal resolver and matcher, so counts, prices, warnings, and available option
18|  lists update together.
19|- Saves are serialized, and cart creation waits for the last edit. Clicking the
20|  cart button immediately after leaving a field therefore cannot build from the
21|  stale value.
22|- Unresolved rows do not disappear. The user may fix them in place or continue;
23|  anything that cannot be added is named in the reconciliation.
24|
25|## After cart creation
26|
27|Cart creation opens a distinct third-step view rather than appending another
28|panel below the order. Its single top back control returns to the saved order
29|review; from there the same control returns to import. The cart handoff view
30|includes a reconciliation with:
31|
32|- requested, placed, and not-placed drink counts;
33|- a person-by-person manifest of every confirmed cart line and its modifiers;
34|- every failed or skipped row, its quantity, and the reason;
35|- the live subtotal, tax, fees, and total when Kung Fu Tea returns them; and
36|- store availability and verification warnings.
37|
38|Successful add responses are checked against the final server-side cart
39|read-back. If an acknowledged line is missing, it moves from the placed manifest
40|to the failure list instead of being presented as safe. The user then opens an
41|editable clone on Kung Fu Tea, compares it with this summary, and performs the
42|manual checkout there. Boba Builder never submits payment.

1|"""Rows -> exact menu items and exact modifier strings. Task 4.
2|
3|    python3 -m app.matcher .runs/<id>.json
4|
5|`app/options.py` got the sheet as far as the store's own words: `Large`, `50%`,
6|`Boba`. That is as far as anything can get without knowing which drink it is,
7|because Kung Fu Tea defines its option groups per item (Task 1 §5) — `Large` is
8|`Large .7` on a Taro Slush, `Large 1` on the next drink along, and the upcharge
9|is part of the string. This module walks the second arrow:
10|
11|    "lg"  ->  "Large"  ->  "Large .7"  on this drink, in this group
12|              options.py   matcher.py
13|
14|and produces, for each row, a line the cart writer can post verbatim.
15|
16|WHAT IT DECIDES, AND WHAT IT REFUSES TO
17|---------------------------------------
18|It applies a drink name three ways, all of which are the *same name*: exactly as
19|written, the same name spelled differently ("Wintermelon Lemonade"), or an alias
20|from `data/mapping.json`. It will not pick between two drinks. A near miss comes
21|back as suggestions on the row and the preview asks a person, because every
22|other axis is a modifier costing pennies and the drink costs a whole drink.
23|
24|For modifiers it is the opposite: it decides, and says what it decided.
25|
26|* **not offered here** — "Large" on a drink sold in one size, `Espresso Shot` on
27|  a drink that doesn't take it. Reported with what that item *does* have, and
28|  dropped rather than guessed at — unless the group is required, where dropping
29|  it would only move the rejection to the store, so the item's own default goes
30|  in and the row says which and why.
31|* **already the default** — 31 Bay Ridge items have no `Regular Sugar 100%` and
32|  66 have no `Regular Ice`. Asking for those is not an impossible request, it is
33|  the recipe: send no modifier (Task 1 §5). Logged, not warned about.
34|* **required, and nobody said** — `Choose A Size` is `min 1` on 136 items and 9
35|  items must pick an included topping, so leaving them out is a rejected order,
36|  not a default. The item's own default is used, or the store's usual from the
37|  mapping file, and the row says so.
38|
39|Nothing here is fatal, and nothing here is silent. A row that can't be matched
40|still reaches the preview with its reasons attached, and the preview can fix any
41|of it in place — see `importer.apply_row_edit`.

111|            "axis": self.axis,

113|            "quantity": self.quantity,
114|            "price": round((self.option.get("price") or 0) * self.quantity, 2),

119|#: import decided long ago which rows are unorderable, and a modifier this store
120|#: can't do is a drink somebody still gets.
121|_LEVEL = {Chosen.NOT_HERE: "warning", Chosen.NO_GROUP: "info",
122|          Chosen.IS_DEFAULT: "info", Chosen.DEFAULTED: "info"}

125|#: Large" and "doesn't do 0% sugar" are both the plain way to say it.
126|_NOT_HERE = {
127|    "size": "doesn't come in {label}",
128|    "sugar": "doesn't do {label} sugar",
129|    "ice": "doesn't do {label}",
130|    "milk": "doesn't do a milk alternative",
131|    "toppings": "doesn't take {label}",
132|}

135|class RowMatcher:
136|    """One row against one menu. Split out so the rules read in one place."""
137|
138|    def __init__(self, store: menu_module.StoreMenu, config: mapping.Mapping,
139|                 columns: dict | None = None):
140|        self.store = store
141|        self.config = config
142|        # Which fields the sheet actually had a column for. A blank Size cell in
143|        # a sheet with a Size column is worth a word; a whole missing column was
144|        # already reported once at the top by the importer.
145|        self.columns = {key.lower() for key in (columns or {})}

149|    def find_item(self, row: dict) -> tuple[menu_module.MenuItem | None, str, list[str]]:
150|        """(item, how it was found, what to offer instead).
151|
152|        The already-resolved name first, then what the sheet said — so the same
153|        three tiers apply whether or not options.py got there first, and a row
154|        somebody corrected by hand looks up the name they picked.
155|        """
156|        canonical = (row.get("canonical") or {}).get("drink") or ""
157|        typed = row.get("drink") or ""

159|                     for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
160|
161|        for text in (canonical, typed):
162|            if not text:
163|                continue
164|            found = self.store.find(text)
165|            if found:
166|                return found.item, "chosen" if chosen else found.how, []
167|            if found.how == menu_module.Match.AMBIGUOUS:
168|                return None, found.how, found.choices
169|        return None, menu_module.Match.NONE, self.store.suggestions(typed)

171|    # -- the modifiers --------------------------------------------------------

173|    def choose(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem, axis: str, label: str) -> Chosen:
174|        """A canonical label -> the exact option on this item, or a reason why not."""
175|        groups = item.groups_for(axis)
176|        required = [group for group in groups if group.required]
177|
178|        if not groups:
179|            if label:
180|                return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NO_GROUP, asked=label,
181|                              message=f"{item.name} has no {_axis_word(axis)} choice, so "
182|                                      f"\"{label}\" wasn't sent")
183|            return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NO_GROUP)
184|
185|        if label:
186|            found = item.literal(axis, label)
187|            if found:
188|                group, option = found
189|                return Chosen(axis, group, option)
190|
191|            offered = item.labels(axis)
192|            phrase = _NOT_HERE.get(axis, "doesn't take {label}").format(label=label)
193|            fallback = self._fallback(required, axis)
194|            if fallback:
195|                # The group is required, so "send nothing" isn't on the table —
196|                # a line missing a required group is a rejected line. Something
197|                # gets ordered and the row says loudly what and why.
198|                group, option = fallback
199|                instead = group.label_for(option["name"])
200|                rest = [name for name in offered if name != instead]
201|                message = (f"{item.name} {phrase} — it only comes {instead}, so that's "
202|                           f"what's ordered") if not rest else (
203|                    f"{item.name} {phrase} — ordered {instead} for now; it also does "
204|                    f"{_join(rest, 'or')}")
205|                return Chosen(axis, group, option, status=Chosen.NOT_HERE,
206|                              choices=offered, asked=label, message=message)
207|            if self._is_the_recipe(axis, label):
208|                # Task 1 §5: no Regular Ice option means regular ice is what you
209|                # get. Sending nothing is the correct order, not a compromise.
210|                return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.IS_DEFAULT,
211|                              message=f"{label.lower()} is how {item.name} comes — "
212|                                      f"no {_axis_word(axis)} sent")
213|            return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NOT_HERE, choices=offered, asked=label,
214|                          message=f"{item.name} {phrase} — it's {_join(offered, 'or')}")
215|
216|        fallback = self._fallback(required, axis)
217|        if fallback:
218|            group, option = fallback
219|            asked = axis in self.columns
220|            return Chosen(axis, group, option, status=Chosen.DEFAULTED,
221|                          message=(f"no {_axis_word(axis)} on this row, so {item.name} "
222|                                   f"is ordered {group.label_for(option['name'])}")
223|                                  if asked else "")
224|        return Chosen(axis)

226|    def _fallback(self, required: list, axis: str):
227|        """(group, option) for the first required group that can fill itself in."""
228|        for group in required:
229|            option = group.default(self.config.required_fallback.get(axis))
230|            if option is not None:
231|                return group, option
232|        return None
233|
234|    def _is_the_recipe(self, axis: str, label: str) -> bool:
235|        return label.lower() in self.config.assumed_defaults.get(axis, ())
236|
237|    def choose_toppings(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem, row: dict) -> list[Chosen]:
238|        canonical = row.get("canonical") or {}
239|        wanted = list(canonical.get("toppings") or [])
240|        counts = canonical.get("topping_quantities") or {}
241|        offered = item.options("toppings")
242|        chosen: list[Chosen] = []
243|
244|        for name in wanted:
245|            found = item.literal("toppings", name)
246|            if not found:
247|                chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", status=Chosen.NOT_HERE, choices=offered,
248|                                     asked=name,
249|                                     message=f"{item.name} doesn't take {name}"
250|                                             if offered else
251|                                             f"{item.name} doesn't take toppings at all"))
252|                continue
253|            group, option = found
254|            count = int(counts.get(name) or 1)
255|            if count > 1 and not group.allows_quantity:
256|                chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, 1,
257|                                     message=f"{item.name} only takes one {name}"))
258|                continue
259|            chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, count))
260|
261|        # An "Included Topping" group is min 1: the drink is defined by it, so a
262|        # sheet that didn't mention it still has to say something.
263|        for group in item.groups_for("toppings"):
264|            if not group.required:
265|                continue
266|            if any(pick.group is group for pick in chosen):
267|                continue
268|            option = group.default()
269|            if option is None:
270|                continue
271|            chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, status=Chosen.DEFAULTED,
272|                                 message=f"{item.name} comes with {option['name']}"))
273|        return chosen
274|
275|    # -- the row --------------------------------------------------------------
276|
277|    def run(self, row: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[Issue]]:
278|        number = row.get("row_number")
279|        issues: list[Issue] = []
280|
281|        def note(chosen: Chosen, field: str) -> None:
282|            level = _LEVEL.get(chosen.status)
283|            if level and chosen.message:
284|                issues.append(Issue(level, chosen.message, field, number,
285|                                    f"{PREFIX}{chosen.status}:{field}"))
286|
287|        if not row.get("ok", True):
288|            return {"status": SKIPPED}, issues
289|
290|        item, how, offer = self.find_item(row)
291|        if item is None:
292|            typed = (row.get("drink") or "").strip()
293|            gone = self.store.unorderable(typed)
294|            message = ""
295|            if how == menu_module.Match.AMBIGUOUS:
296|                message = f"\"{typed}\" is two different drinks here — {_join(offer, 'or')}"
297|            elif gone is not None:
298|                message = (f"{gone.name} is sold out today" if gone.sold_out
299|                           else f"{gone.name} isn't something this can order")
300|                offer = offer or self.store.suggestions(typed)
301|            elif not _already_said(row, "drink"):
302|                # options.py says "no drink called X — did you mean Y?" while
303|                # resolving the row. Saying it again in different words would
304|                # only make the preview look like two things went wrong.
305|                message = f"no drink called \"{typed}\" on this store's menu"
306|                if offer:
307|                    message += f" — did you mean {_join(offer[:2], 'or')}?"
308|            if message:
309|                issues.append(Issue("warning", message, "drink", number,
310|                                    f"{PREFIX}no-item"))
311|            return {"status": NEEDS_DRINK, "choices": {"drink": offer}}, issues
312|
313|        canonical = row.get("canonical") or {}
314|        picks = [self.choose(item, "size", canonical.get("size") or ""),
315|                 self.choose(item, "sugar", canonical.get("sugar") or ""),
316|                 self.choose(item, "ice", canonical.get("ice") or ""),
317|                 self.choose(item, "milk", canonical.get("milk") or "")]
318|        for pick in picks:
319|            note(pick, pick.axis)
320|        toppings = self.choose_toppings(item, row)
321|        for pick in toppings:
322|            note(pick, "toppings")
323|        picks += toppings
324|
325|        line_options = [entry for entry in
326|                        (pick.as_option() for pick in picks) if entry]
327|        quantity = int(row.get("quantity") or 1)
328|        unit = float(item.base_price or 0)
329|        extras = round(sum(entry["price"] for entry in line_options), 2)
330|
331|        # Two different bad outcomes, and the page shows them differently: one
332|        # is a decision waiting to be made, the other is a request this drink
333|        # simply can't take, with nothing to choose between.
334|        unmapped = [{"axis": pick.axis, "asked": pick.asked, "why": pick.message}
335|                    for pick in picks if pick.status == Chosen.NOT_HERE]

338|        choices = {pick.axis: pick.choices for pick in picks if pick.choices}

340|        return {
341|            "status": READY,
342|            "matched_by": how,
343|            "item": item.as_dict(),
344|            "price_tier": item.price_tier,
345|            "quantity": quantity,
346|            "options": line_options,
347|            "unit_price": round(unit, 2),
348|            "extras_price": extras,
349|            "total": round((unit + extras) * quantity, 2),
350|            "unmapped": unmapped,
351|            "dropped": dropped,
352|            "choices": choices,
353|            "available": self.available(item),
354|        }, issues
355|
356|    def available(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem) -> dict:
357|        """Everything this one drink can be ordered with, per axis.
358|
359|        `choices` is only the axes that went wrong. This is the whole list, so
360|        the review screen can offer a dropdown of what is actually possible for
361|        this drink rather than the store's vocabulary as a whole — the two are
362|        very different (a slush has no ice level at all).
363|        """
364|        return {
365|            "size": item.labels("size"),
366|            "sugar": item.labels("sugar"),
367|            "ice": item.labels("ice"),
368|            "milk": item.labels("milk"),
369|            "toppings": item.options("toppings"),

373|def _already_said(row: dict, field: str) -> bool:
374|    """Has app/options.py already flagged this field on this row?"""
375|    return any(str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith("option:")
376|               and issue.get("field") == field
377|               for issue in row.get("issues") or [])

382|            "milk": "milk alternative", "toppings": "topping"}.get(axis, axis)

388|def match(run: dict, store: menu_module.StoreMenu | None = None) -> dict:
389|    """Add a menu match to every row of a saved import. The Task 4 stage.
390|
391|    Pure: it reads the run and the menu snapshot and returns a new run. Running
392|    it twice on the same input gives the same answer — its own notes are cleared
393|    first — so the preview can re-derive it on every read rather than storing a
394|    result that goes stale the moment somebody corrects a row.
395|    """
396|    # `is None`, not `or`: an empty menu is falsy and must stay the one we were
397|    # handed, so "there is no snapshot" is reported rather than papered over.
398|    restaurant_id = (run.get("source") or {}).get("restaurant_id")
399|    store = menu_module.store_menu(restaurant_id) if store is None else store
400|    config = store.config
401|    matcher = RowMatcher(store, config, run.get("column_map"))

403|    result = dict(run)
404|    rows: list[dict] = []
405|    # Our own notes go first, so re-matching replaces them rather than stacking
406|    # them up. options.py's "N drinks didn't match by name" goes too: it is the
407|    # same fact counted without the menu in hand, and this stage recounts it.
408|    issues = [issue for issue in run.get("issues") or []
409|              if not str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith(PREFIX)
410|              and issue.get("code") != "option:unmatched-drinks"]
411|
412|    if not store:
413|        rows = [dict(row, match={"status": SKIPPED}) for row in run.get("rows") or []]
414|        issues.append(Issue("warning", "there's no menu snapshot for this store, so "
415|                                       "nothing could be matched to it — run "
416|                                       "scripts/fetch_menu.py", None, None,
417|                            f"{PREFIX}no-menu").as_dict())
418|        result["rows"] = rows
419|        result["issues"] = issues
420|        result["match"] = {"ready": 0, "needs_drink": 0, "skipped": len(rows)}
421|        return result
422|
423|    ready = 0
424|    drinks = 0
425|    subtotal = 0.0
426|    for row in run.get("rows") or []:
427|        row = dict(row)
428|        row["issues"] = [issue for issue in row.get("issues") or []
429|                         if not str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith(PREFIX)]
430|        found, row_issues = matcher.run(row)
431|        row["issues"] += [issue.as_dict() for issue in row_issues]
432|        row["match"] = found
433|        if found["status"] == READY:
434|            ready += 1
435|            drinks += found["quantity"]
436|            subtotal += found["total"]
437|        rows.append(row)
438|
439|    # A preview flag means "look at this row", not only "the drink name did not
440|    # match". Include parser warnings and requests this particular drink cannot
441|    # take, even when the remaining line is still safe to add to a cart.
442|    attention = sum(
443|        1 for row in rows
444|        if (row.get("match") or {}).get("status") != READY
445|        or any(issue.get("level") in ("warning", "error")
446|               for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
447|        or bool((row.get("match") or {}).get("unmapped"))
448|        or bool((row.get("match") or {}).get("dropped"))
449|    )
450|
451|    unmatched = sum(1 for row in rows if row["match"]["status"] == NEEDS_DRINK)
452|    if unmatched:
453|        issues.append(Issue(
454|            "warning",
455|            f"{unmatched} drink{'s' if unmatched != 1 else ''} still need"
456|            f"{'' if unmatched != 1 else 's'} picking from the menu before the cart "
457|            f"can be built", "drink", None, f"{PREFIX}unmatched").as_dict())
458|
459|    captured = menu_module.captured_at(store.restaurant_id)
460|    age = (_dt.date.today() - captured).days if captured else None
461|    if age is not None and age > config.menu_stale_days:
462|        # Task 1 §6: options are addressed by name, so a rename breaks the cart
463|        # quietly. An old snapshot is the one way this stage is wrong without

465|        issues.append(Issue(
466|            "info", f"this menu was captured {age} days ago — re-run "
467|                    f"scripts/fetch_menu.py if the cart starts rejecting options",

470|    result["rows"] = rows
471|    result["issues"] = issues
472|    result["match"] = {
473|        "store": store.store,
474|        "restaurant_id": store.restaurant_id,
475|        "menu_items": len(store.drinks),
476|        "menu_captured": captured.isoformat() if captured else None,
477|        # What the whole store offers, for a row whose drink isn't picked yet.
478|        # Once it is, the row's own `match.available` is the narrower truth.
479|        "vocabulary": store.vocabulary(),
480|        "ready": ready,
481|        "needs_drink": unmatched,
482|        "skipped": sum(1 for row in rows if row["match"]["status"] == SKIPPED),
483|        "needs_attention": attention,
484|        "drinks": drinks,
485|        "subtotal": round(subtotal, 2),
486|    }
487|    cart = result.get("cart") or {}
488|    result["costs"] = (costs.from_cart(cart) if cart.get("review_ready")
489|                       else costs.from_rows(rows))

1|"""Rows -> exact menu items and exact modifier strings. Task 4.
2|
3|    python3 -m app.matcher .runs/<id>.json
4|
5|`app/options.py` got the sheet as far as the store's own words: `Large`, `50%`,
6|`Boba`. That is as far as anything can get without knowing which drink it is,
7|because Kung Fu Tea defines its option groups per item (Task 1 §5) — `Large` is
8|`Large .7` on a Taro Slush, `Large 1` on the next drink along, and the upcharge
9|is part of the string. This module walks the second arrow:
10|
11|    "lg"  ->  "Large"  ->  "Large .7"  on this drink, in this group
12|              options.py   matcher.py
13|
14|and produces, for each row, a line the cart writer can post verbatim.
15|
16|WHAT IT DECIDES, AND WHAT IT REFUSES TO
17|---------------------------------------
18|It applies a drink name three ways, all of which are the *same name*: exactly as
19|written, the same name spelled differently ("Wintermelon Lemonade"), or an alias
20|from `data/mapping.json`. It will not pick between two drinks. A near miss comes
21|back as suggestions on the row and the preview asks a person, because every
22|other axis is a modifier costing pennies and the drink costs a whole drink.
23|
24|For modifiers it is the opposite: it decides, and says what it decided.
25|
26|* **not offered here** — "Large" on a drink sold in one size, `Espresso Shot` on
27|  a drink that doesn't take it. Reported with what that item *does* have, and
28|  dropped rather than guessed at — unless the group is required, where dropping
29|  it would only move the rejection to the store, so the item's own default goes
30|  in and the row says which and why.
31|* **already the default** — 31 Bay Ridge items have no `Regular Sugar 100%` and
32|  66 have no `Regular Ice`. Asking for those is not an impossible request, it is
33|  the recipe: send no modifier (Task 1 §5). Logged, not warned about.
34|* **required, and nobody said** — `Choose A Size` is `min 1` on 136 items and 9
35|  items must pick an included topping, so leaving them out is a rejected order,
36|  not a default. The item's own default is used, or the store's usual from the
37|  mapping file, and the row says so.
38|
39|Nothing here is fatal, and nothing here is silent. A row that can't be matched
40|still reaches the preview with its reasons attached, and the preview can fix any
41|of it in place — see `importer.apply_row_edit`.

111|            "axis": self.axis,
112|            "name": self.option["name"],
113|            "quantity": self.quantity,
114|            "price": round((self.option.get("price") or 0) * self.quantity, 2),

135|class RowMatcher:
136|    """One row against one menu. Split out so the rules read in one place."""
137|
138|    def __init__(self, store: menu_module.StoreMenu, config: mapping.Mapping,
139|                 columns: dict | None = None):
140|        self.store = store
141|        self.config = config
142|        # Which fields the sheet actually had a column for. A blank Size cell in
143|        # a sheet with a Size column is worth a word; a whole missing column was
144|        # already reported once at the top by the importer.
145|        self.columns = {key.lower() for key in (columns or {})}
146|
147|    # -- the drink ------------------------------------------------------------
148|
149|    def find_item(self, row: dict) -> tuple[menu_module.MenuItem | None, str, list[str]]:
150|        """(item, how it was found, what to offer instead).
151|
152|        The already-resolved name first, then what the sheet said — so the same
153|        three tiers apply whether or not options.py got there first, and a row
154|        somebody corrected by hand looks up the name they picked.
155|        """
156|        canonical = (row.get("canonical") or {}).get("drink") or ""
157|        typed = row.get("drink") or ""
158|        chosen = any((issue.get("code") or "") == "edited:drink"
159|                     for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
160|
161|        for text in (canonical, typed):
162|            if not text:
163|                continue
164|            found = self.store.find(text)
165|            if found:
166|                return found.item, "chosen" if chosen else found.how, []
167|            if found.how == menu_module.Match.AMBIGUOUS:
168|                return None, found.how, found.choices
169|        return None, menu_module.Match.NONE, self.store.suggestions(typed)

171|    # -- the modifiers --------------------------------------------------------
172|
173|    def choose(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem, axis: str, label: str) -> Chosen:
174|        """A canonical label -> the exact option on this item, or a reason why not."""
175|        groups = item.groups_for(axis)
176|        required = [group for group in groups if group.required]
177|
178|        if not groups:
179|            if label:
180|                return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NO_GROUP, asked=label,
181|                              message=f"{item.name} has no {_axis_word(axis)} choice, so "
182|                                      f"\"{label}\" wasn't sent")
183|            return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NO_GROUP)
184|
185|        if label:
186|            found = item.literal(axis, label)
187|            if found:
188|                group, option = found
189|                return Chosen(axis, group, option)
190|
191|            offered = item.labels(axis)
192|            phrase = _NOT_HERE.get(axis, "doesn't take {label}").format(label=label)
193|            fallback = self._fallback(required, axis)
194|            if fallback:
195|                # The group is required, so "send nothing" isn't on the table —
196|                # a line missing a required group is a rejected line. Something
197|                # gets ordered and the row says loudly what and why.
198|                group, option = fallback
199|                instead = group.label_for(option["name"])
200|                rest = [name for name in offered if name != instead]
201|                message = (f"{item.name} {phrase} — it only comes {instead}, so that's "
202|                           f"what's ordered") if not rest else (
203|                    f"{item.name} {phrase} — ordered {instead} for now; it also does "
204|                    f"{_join(rest, 'or')}")
205|                return Chosen(axis, group, option, status=Chosen.NOT_HERE,
206|                              choices=offered, asked=label, message=message)
207|            if self._is_the_recipe(axis, label):
208|                # Task 1 §5: no Regular Ice option means regular ice is what you
209|                # get. Sending nothing is the correct order, not a compromise.
210|                return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.IS_DEFAULT,
211|                              message=f"{label.lower()} is how {item.name} comes — "
212|                                      f"no {_axis_word(axis)} sent")
213|            return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NOT_HERE, choices=offered, asked=label,
214|                          message=f"{item.name} {phrase} — it's {_join(offered, 'or')}")
215|
216|        fallback = self._fallback(required, axis)
217|        if fallback:
218|            group, option = fallback
219|            asked = axis in self.columns
220|            return Chosen(axis, group, option, status=Chosen.DEFAULTED,
221|                          message=(f"no {_axis_word(axis)} on this row, so {item.name} "
222|                                   f"is ordered {group.label_for(option['name'])}")
223|                                  if asked else "")
224|        return Chosen(axis)
225|
226|    def _fallback(self, required: list, axis: str):
227|        """(group, option) for the first required group that can fill itself in."""
228|        for group in required:
229|            option = group.default(self.config.required_fallback.get(axis))
230|            if option is not None:
231|                return group, option
232|        return None
233|
234|    def _is_the_recipe(self, axis: str, label: str) -> bool:
235|        return label.lower() in self.config.assumed_defaults.get(axis, ())
236|
237|    def choose_toppings(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem, row: dict) -> list[Chosen]:
238|        canonical = row.get("canonical") or {}
239|        wanted = list(canonical.get("toppings") or [])
240|        counts = canonical.get("topping_quantities") or {}
241|        offered = item.options("toppings")
242|        chosen: list[Chosen] = []
243|
244|        for name in wanted:
245|            found = item.literal("toppings", name)
246|            if not found:
247|                chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", status=Chosen.NOT_HERE, choices=offered,
248|                                     asked=name,
249|                                     message=f"{item.name} doesn't take {name}"
250|                                             if offered else
251|                                             f"{item.name} doesn't take toppings at all"))
252|                continue
253|            group, option = found
254|            count = int(counts.get(name) or 1)
255|            if count > 1 and not group.allows_quantity:
256|                chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, 1,
257|                                     message=f"{item.name} only takes one {name}"))
258|                continue
259|            chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, count))
260|
261|        # An "Included Topping" group is min 1: the drink is defined by it, so a
262|        # sheet that didn't mention it still has to say something.
263|        for group in item.groups_for("toppings"):
264|            if not group.required:
265|                continue
266|            if any(pick.group is group for pick in chosen):
267|                continue
268|            option = group.default()
269|            if option is None:
270|                continue
271|            chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, status=Chosen.DEFAULTED,
272|                                 message=f"{item.name} comes with {option['name']}"))
273|        return chosen
274|
275|    # -- the row --------------------------------------------------------------
276|
277|    def run(self, row: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[Issue]]:
278|        number = row.get("row_number")
279|        issues: list[Issue] = []
280|
281|        def note(chosen: Chosen, field: str) -> None:
282|            level = _LEVEL.get(chosen.status)
283|            if level and chosen.message:
284|                issues.append(Issue(level, chosen.message, field, number,
285|                                    f"{PREFIX}{chosen.status}:{field}"))
286|
287|        if not row.get("ok", True):
288|            return {"status": SKIPPED}, issues
289|
290|        item, how, offer = self.find_item(row)
291|        if item is None:
292|            typed = (row.get("drink") or "").strip()
293|            gone = self.store.unorderable(typed)
294|            message = ""
295|            if how == menu_module.Match.AMBIGUOUS:
296|                message = f"\"{typed}\" is two different drinks here — {_join(offer, 'or')}"
297|            elif gone is not None:
298|                message = (f"{gone.name} is sold out today" if gone.sold_out
299|                           else f"{gone.name} isn't something this can order")
300|                offer = offer or self.store.suggestions(typed)
301|            elif not _already_said(row, "drink"):
302|                # options.py says "no drink called X — did you mean Y?" while
303|                # resolving the row. Saying it again in different words would
304|                # only make the preview look like two things went wrong.
305|                message = f"no drink called \"{typed}\" on this store's menu"
306|                if offer:
307|                    message += f" — did you mean {_join(offer[:2], 'or')}?"
308|            if message:
309|                issues.append(Issue("warning", message, "drink", number,
310|                                    f"{PREFIX}no-item"))
311|            return {"status": NEEDS_DRINK, "choices": {"drink": offer}}, issues
312|
313|        canonical = row.get("canonical") or {}
314|        picks = [self.choose(item, "size", canonical.get("size") or ""),
315|                 self.choose(item, "sugar", canonical.get("sugar") or ""),
316|                 self.choose(item, "ice", canonical.get("ice") or ""),
317|                 self.choose(item, "milk", canonical.get("milk") or "")]
318|        for pick in picks:
319|            note(pick, pick.axis)
320|        toppings = self.choose_toppings(item, row)
321|        for pick in toppings:
322|            note(pick, "toppings")
323|        picks += toppings
324|
325|        line_options = [entry for entry in
326|                        (pick.as_option() for pick in picks) if entry]
327|        quantity = int(row.get("quantity") or 1)
328|        unit = float(item.base_price or 0)
329|        extras = round(sum(entry["price"] for entry in line_options), 2)
330|
331|        # Two different bad outcomes, and the page shows them differently: one
332|        # is a decision waiting to be made, the other is a request this drink
333|        # simply can't take, with nothing to choose between.
334|        unmapped = [{"axis": pick.axis, "asked": pick.asked, "why": pick.message}
335|                    for pick in picks if pick.status == Chosen.NOT_HERE]
336|        dropped = [{"axis": pick.axis, "asked": pick.asked, "why": pick.message}
337|                   for pick in picks if pick.status == Chosen.NO_GROUP and pick.asked]
338|        choices = {pick.axis: pick.choices for pick in picks if pick.choices}
339|
340|        return {
341|            "status": READY,
342|            "matched_by": how,
343|            "item": item.as_dict(),
344|            "price_tier": item.price_tier,
345|            "quantity": quantity,
346|            "options": line_options,
347|            "unit_price": round(unit, 2),
348|            "extras_price": extras,
349|            "total": round((unit + extras) * quantity, 2),
350|            "unmapped": unmapped,
351|            "dropped": dropped,
352|            "choices": choices,
353|            "available": self.available(item),
354|        }, issues
355|
356|    def available(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem) -> dict:
357|        """Everything this one drink can be ordered with, per axis.
358|
359|        `choices` is only the axes that went wrong. This is the whole list, so
360|        the review screen can offer a dropdown of what is actually possible for
361|        this drink rather than the store's vocabulary as a whole — the two are
362|        very different (a slush has no ice level at all).
363|        """
364|        return {
365|            "size": item.labels("size"),
366|            "sugar": item.labels("sugar"),
367|            "ice": item.labels("ice"),
368|            "milk": item.labels("milk"),
369|            "toppings": item.options("toppings"),
370|        }
371|
372|
373|def _already_said(row: dict, field: str) -> bool:
374|    """Has app/options.py already flagged this field on this row?"""
375|    return any(str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith("option:")
376|               and issue.get("field") == field
377|               for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
378|
379|
380|def _axis_word(axis: str) -> str:
381|    return {"size": "size", "sugar": "sugar level", "ice": "ice level",
382|            "milk": "milk alternative", "toppings": "topping"}.get(axis, axis)

385|# --- the pipeline stage ------------------------------------------------------

387|
388|def match(run: dict, store: menu_module.StoreMenu | None = None) -> dict:
389|    """Add a menu match to every row of a saved import. The Task 4 stage.
390|
391|    Pure: it reads the run and the menu snapshot and returns a new run. Running
392|    it twice on the same input gives the same answer — its own notes are cleared
393|    first — so the preview can re-derive it on every read rather than storing a
394|    result that goes stale the moment somebody corrects a row.
395|    """
396|    # `is None`, not `or`: an empty menu is falsy and must stay the one we were
397|    # handed, so "there is no snapshot" is reported rather than papered over.
398|    restaurant_id = (run.get("source") or {}).get("restaurant_id")
399|    store = menu_module.store_menu(restaurant_id) if store is None else store
400|    config = store.config
401|    matcher = RowMatcher(store, config, run.get("column_map"))
402|
403|    result = dict(run)
404|    rows: list[dict] = []
405|    # Our own notes go first, so re-matching replaces them rather than stacking
406|    # them up. options.py's "N drinks didn't match by name" goes too: it is the
407|    # same fact counted without the menu in hand, and this stage recounts it.
408|    issues = [issue for issue in run.get("issues") or []
409|              if not str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith(PREFIX)
410|              and issue.get("code") != "option:unmatched-drinks"]
411|
412|    if not store:
413|        rows = [dict(row, match={"status": SKIPPED}) for row in run.get("rows") or []]
414|        issues.append(Issue("warning", "there's no menu snapshot for this store, so "
415|                                       "nothing could be matched to it — run "
416|                                       "scripts/fetch_menu.py", None, None,
417|                            f"{PREFIX}no-menu").as_dict())
418|        result["rows"] = rows
419|        result["issues"] = issues
420|        result["match"] = {"ready": 0, "needs_drink": 0, "skipped": len(rows)}
421|        return result
422|
423|    ready = 0
424|    drinks = 0
425|    subtotal = 0.0
426|    for row in run.get("rows") or []:
427|        row = dict(row)
428|        row["issues"] = [issue for issue in row.get("issues") or []
429|                         if not str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith(PREFIX)]
430|        found, row_issues = matcher.run(row)
431|        row["issues"] += [issue.as_dict() for issue in row_issues]
432|        row["match"] = found

435|            drinks += found["quantity"]
436|            subtotal += found["total"]
437|        rows.append(row)

439|    # A preview flag means "look at this row", not only "the drink name did not
440|    # match". Include parser warnings and requests this particular drink cannot
441|    # take, even when the remaining line is still safe to add to a cart.
442|    attention = sum(
443|        1 for row in rows
444|        if (row.get("match") or {}).get("status") != READY
445|        or any(issue.get("level") in ("warning", "error")
446|               for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
447|        or bool((row.get("match") or {}).get("unmapped"))
448|        or bool((row.get("match") or {}).get("dropped"))
449|    )
450|
451|    unmatched = sum(1 for row in rows if row["match"]["status"] == NEEDS_DRINK)
452|    if unmatched:
453|        issues.append(Issue(
454|            "warning",
455|            f"{unmatched} drink{'s' if unmatched != 1 else ''} still need"
456|            f"{'' if unmatched != 1 else 's'} picking from the menu before the cart "
457|            f"can be built", "drink", None, f"{PREFIX}unmatched").as_dict())
458|
459|    captured = menu_module.captured_at(store.restaurant_id)
460|    age = (_dt.date.today() - captured).days if captured else None

462|        # Task 1 §6: options are addressed by name, so a rename breaks the cart
463|        # quietly. An old snapshot is the one way this stage is wrong without

465|        issues.append(Issue(

467|                    f"scripts/fetch_menu.py if the cart starts rejecting options",
468|            None, None, f"{PREFIX}stale-menu").as_dict())
469|
470|    result["rows"] = rows
471|    result["issues"] = issues
472|    result["match"] = {
473|        "store": store.store,
474|        "restaurant_id": store.restaurant_id,
475|        "menu_items": len(store.drinks),
476|        "menu_captured": captured.isoformat() if captured else None,

482|        "skipped": sum(1 for row in rows if row["match"]["status"] == SKIPPED),
483|        "needs_attention": attention,
484|        "drinks": drinks,
485|        "subtotal": round(subtotal, 2),

487|    cart = result.get("cart") or {}
488|    result["costs"] = (costs.from_cart(cart) if cart.get("review_ready")

  overwriting one another.

  multi-process deployment should use a transactional database.

----------------------
- Each submitted drink is stored as an order line containing the person's
  display name, drink, modifiers, quantity, notes, and timestamps.

  count, total drink quantity, distinct person count, and totals by person.

Trajectories not helpful. Need actual GET order payload. From task1 recommendation: source: Thai Tea + Taro Slush, clone options preserved exactly: "Choose A Size: Large .5 | Choose Topping(s): Brown Sugar Wow Boba x1, Sugar Level: Half S 50%, Ice Level: Less Ice". And verify_handoff prints i["name"], i["total_price"], [o["name"] for o in i.get("options",[])].

So GET order items have: id (line id), name, total_price, options: list of {name,...?}, probably also quantity, menu item id? Need to check real response shape. Could look at docs/api-endpoints or fetch_menu? Alternatively search codebase for item fields used: cart.py uses added.get("id"), added.get("total_price"); order.get("items"), item.get("id"). _manifest_entry stores cart_item_id = added.get("id"), actual_total = added.get("total_price").

Also add_item returns result with id, name, quantity, total_price (FakeApi). Real API add_item response? Unknown but presumably similar.

For verification design, I need to be defensive: site representation may differ — item ids may be menu item ids vs line ids, options may be nested differently, quantities may be merged.

Task requirements recap:
- After building cart, verify actual contents against what app intended to order.
- Don't trust build process's own report of success — verify against reality. Once cart assembled, read back what's actually in it and compare against set of orders app intended to place.
- Discrepancies: missing items, wrong or dropped modifiers, incorrect quantities, unexpected extras.
- Decide how you obtain true cart state given handoff mechanism Task 1 established, and how you match cart entries back to intended orders when site's representation doesn't align 1:1.
- Present mismatch to organizer in form they can act on at moment it matters — right before payment.
- Posture when verification itself fails or inconclusive: claiming cart correct when couldn't confirm is worse than saying plainly.

Design:

True cart state: GET api/v1/orders/{source_order_id} immediately after build + quote (already done in cart.build). That's the source order; the user's clone will be derived from it server-side. We cannot read the user's clone (different session, no token, and clone happens later in their browser). So document this: verification covers source cart; clone fidelity was verified in Task 1 (options preserved, for/notes dropped by design). Also note cross-check: optionally perform server-side clone_order + read clone to verify clone fidelity? Task 1 says clone_order is exactly what browser does. But doing a clone per build would create extra orders; maybe not. Better: verify source order read-back thoroughly; treat clone as covered by Task 1 findings + warn that user edits after handoff aren't visible to us.

Actually, could we verify via clone? The handoff doc says clone drops for/notes — expected. Cloning on every build doubles orders and could confuse? Probably not desirable. Keep verification on source read-back.

Matching: site's representation doesn't align 1:1:
- identical drinks for different people collapse into indistinguishable line items (Task 1 §4) — plus server may merge same-config lines or keep separate line ids.
- per-item for/notes dropped in clone (expected, not a discrepancy on source read; but if verifying clone, ignore those).
- option names include price suffixes; compare normalized? We posted exact literals, so compare exact names but normalize whitespace/case defensively.
- quantities: user asked quantity N on one row → server may represent as one line with quantity N or N lines of quantity 1. Handle both by aggregating quantities per (item, options) key.
- extras: server may add fees/totals differences — compare line-level, not just totals.

So verification algorithm: build expected multiset from added_manifest (intended lines that were acknowledged): key = (menu item id or name, normalized options multiset incl. quantities, line quantity). Build actual multiset from GET order items: each item → (menu item ref, options, quantity). Match greedily: for each expected entry, find an actual entry with same item + same options + sufficient quantity. Report:
- missing: expected with no actual match (or short quantity)
- modifier mismatch: same item+person but options differ (wrong/dropped modifiers)
- quantity mismatch: same item+options but quantity differs
- unexpected: actual entries with no expected counterpart (extras)

Need actual item field names. Must inspect real API response. Can we call live API? Possibly network available? Let's try a safe read-only call? Creating orders is human-scale allowed per Task 1. But verification should not require live network in tests. Let's try GET menu / create+read a test order? Task 1 says test carts expire, allowed. But careful: don't submit. A create+add+read+leave unsubmitted is within established usage. Could do it to learn the true shape.

Alternatively design verification to be shape-tolerant: extract item identity from multiple possible fields (menu item id fields: item_id, menuitem_id, menu_item_id, id when it looks like menu id vs line id...). Hmm but line id vs menu id ambiguity: added.get("id") is line id; order items' id is also line id (confirmed_ids check compares them). So order item id = line id. Menu item identity must come from another field: e.g., item.get("menuitem_id") or item.get("item_id") or item.get("id")? But existing code treats item.get("id") as line id (confirmed_ids = {str(item.get("id"))}). So menu identity needs separate field. What does GET order item contain for menu ref? Unknown. From verify_handoff: i["name"], i["total_price"], [o["name"] for o in i.get("options",[])]. No menu id shown. Possibly item has "menuitem_id" or "item_id" or nested "menuitem". Need to discover.

Let's try live API read: create order, add item, get order, print full JSON. That's the honest way to learn shape. Check network availability first.

Also need to check app/menu.py for live_store_menu shape, app/costs.py, tests/test_preview_js.py to see JS test harness, and app.css for styling classes.

Plan:
1. Probe live API shape (read-only + one throwaway cart, unsubmitted, as Task 1 established).
2. Implement app/verify.py (or extend cart.py?) with verify_cart(expected_manifest, order) → verification dict.
3. Wire into cart.build: after read-back, run verification; store in cart["verification"]; on mismatch, move affected lines? Or keep manifest but flag? Task says surface discrepancy before organizer pays. Options: mark cart status partial? Or keep ready but verification status warns? Need to think: existing statuses ready/partial/failed. Verification mismatch should probably downgrade ready→partial? Hmm, but partial currently means some rows not added. A modifier mismatch on an otherwise-added line is similar severity. I think: verification result has status: matched | mismatched | unverified (couldn't confirm). If mismatched, set cart status to partial? But cart.status partial already used. Alternatively keep cart.status but add verification block and surface prominently; organizer acts by rebuilding/editing. Let's look at how preview renders status: ready → "ready to review", partial → "ready, with a few drinks left out", failed → "could not be made". If modifiers wrong but all lines present, "ready" with a warning panel might understate. Better to downgrade to partial when verification finds missing/quantity/modifier problems, and add failed entries? But failed entries currently represent rows not added; a wrong-modifier line IS added but wrong. Hmm.

Alternative cleaner: keep added list as confirmed lines, add verification:{status, checked_at, source, mismatches[], unexpected[], unverified...} and let UI render a dedicated "Cart check" panel with actionable per-line messages + extent. And if mismatches exist, set a flag cart["needs_review"]? Let me look at what tests expect and minimal disruption: existing test expects status partial when a line missing from read-back, with failed code verification_failed. For deeper mismatches, similar: mark affected expected lines? But a modifier-mismatch line is present — moving it to failed would miscount added_drinks. Perhaps keep it in added but annotate? Or move to failed with code like modifier_mismatch?

I think best: verification compares and produces:
{
  "status": "matched" | "mismatched" | "unverified",
  "source": "source_order" (+ order_id),
  "checked_at": iso,
  "note": human sentence,
  "mismatches": [{row_number, person, drink, quantity, kind: missing|quantity|modifiers|unexpected, expected:..., actual:..., detail}],
  "unexpected": [...],
  "unverified_reason" (when unverified)
}
And cart.build behavior:
- if order read-back failed (order={}) → verification unverified; keep existing warning; review_ready stays true (handoff useful) but UI must say totals/contents couldn't be confirmed. (Current code already warns "totals could not be verified".)
- if order_items not a list → unverified similarly.
- if mismatches → keep lines in added (they're in the cart, organizer will see them in clone), but set cart status: if previously "ready" → "partial"? Hmm that changes counts semantics. Alternatively add cart["verification"] and let UI show blocking-style panel while keeping status. The task says "Present any mismatch to the organizer in a form they can act on at the moment it matters — right before payment." The moment is the cart handoff view, next to the "Open the cart at Kung Fu Tea" button. A dedicated panel with per-drink actions (edit row & rebuild, or fix in Kung Fu Tea clone) suffices; status downgrade optional.

But "Decide ... how you match cart entries back to intended orders when the site's representation doesn't align one-to-one" — must handle aggregation: match by (item name/id + options) aggregated quantities, not by line id. The current confirmed_ids check is line-id-based and fragile if server merges lines. New verifier should do semantic matching, with line-id confirmation as a fast path/fallback.

Also totals check: compare expected subtotal (sum of manifest actual_total or estimated) vs order subtotal; flag drift beyond tolerance (e.g., $0.01 rounding vs real price change). Price drift risk noted in Task 1 §7. Include totals comparison with tolerance.

event.text: Designing a pure verification function that aggregates expected and actual items by key and compares quantities, options, and totals.
Designing a pure verification function that aggregates expected and actual items by key and compares quantities, options, and totals.

Confirmed live (2026-09-21):
- Clone preserves menuitem, options (group_name/option_name/quantity), quantity, prices. Drops for/notes.
- quantity is a string in GET; coerce.
- options identified by (group_name, option_name, quantity).

Now design Task 24 implementation:

**New module `app/verify.py`**: `verify(expected_manifest, order)` → verification dict. Pure function, testable with fakes.

Expected manifest entries (from cart._manifest_entry): row_number, person, drink, quantity, item_id, price_tier, options [{group, axis, name, quantity}], notes, estimated_total, cart_item_id, actual_total.

Actual items: {id (line), menuitem (menu id), name, quantity (str|int), options [{group_name, option_name, quantity, ...}], total_price, size}.

Matching strategy (handles non-1:1):
1. Aggregate actual lines by key (menuitem or normalized name, options multiset). Aggregate expected lines likewise BUT keep per-row identity for reporting: match per expected entry against pool of actual quantity.
   - Actually per-row reporting matters ("Alice's Taro Slush is missing"). Approach: for each expected entry in order, consume matching actual quantity from pool keyed by (item, options). If pool has same-item with different options → modifier mismatch detail (show expected vs actual option sets). If pool has same item+options but insufficient quantity → quantity shortfall. Leftover actual quantity → unexpected extras.
2. Normalization: option key = (group_name.strip().lower(), option_name.strip().lower(), qty). Item key = menuitem id when present else normalized name. Compare case-insensitively, strip whitespace — defensive against server re-spelling (e.g., "Boba x1" combined names — use option_name/group_name fields, fall back to parsing "Group: Opt" name).
3. Totals: compare expected subtotal (sum actual_total or estimated_total over expected) vs order subtotal with tolerance $0.05? Actually actual_total comes from add responses; subtotal should equal sum. Flag if abs diff > $0.01... server rounds; use 0.02? Keep simple: flag drift > $0.01 and report. Hmm live: subtotal 20 = 7.4+12.6 exact. Use tolerance 0.015 to avoid float noise, round to 2dp first.

Verification statuses:
- "matched": every expected line matched in full, no extras, totals agree.
- "mismatched": any missing/short/modifier-mismatch/extra/totals-drift.
- "unverified": order missing, items not a list, or read failed — cannot confirm. Never claim correct.

Mismatch entry shape (actionable):
{
  "kind": "missing" | "short_quantity" | "modifiers" | "unexpected" | "totals",
  "row_number" (when attributable), "person", "drink", "quantity" (expected),
  "expected": "Large .7 · Boba ×2 · Half S 50%" (human string),
  "actual": "..." or "not in the cart",
  "detail": "sentence the organizer can act on",
  "action": "edit the row and rebuild, or fix it in the Kung Fu Tea cart before paying"
}

Hmm, keep action generic per kind.

**Wire into `app/cart.py` build()**:
- Replace/augment the existing confirmed_ids-only check with verify.verify(added_manifest, order).
- Keep backward-compatible behavior: missing lines (no line-id match AND no semantic match) → move to failed with code "verification_failed" (existing test expects this). New: modifier/quantity mismatches → keep line in added? or move to failed?

Decision: A line with wrong modifiers or short quantity is *in the cart but wrong* — organizer must fix before paying. Moving it to failed with codes "modifier_mismatch"/"quantity_mismatch" makes counts honest? But counts.added_drinks counts drinks added; a wrong-modifier drink is still a drink in cart. Hmm. Existing semantics: added = manifest of confirmed cart lines; failed = named rows not in cart. A wrong line is arguably "not placed as ordered". I'll keep the line in `added` (so manifest + pickup labels + costs stay consistent with the real cart) and record the problem in `verification.mismatches` with row attribution, plus add a warning string. And downgrade status ready→partial? "partial" currently signals "a few drinks left out". A wrong-modifier cart is also not fully right... but changing status could break existing tests? Existing tests: ready when all added & no failed. If verification mismatched occurs only in new scenarios, no existing test breaks. But is downgrade right? The task says "surface any discrepancy before the organizer pays" — a prominent verification panel does that. Downgrading to partial also changes review_ready? No, review_ready stays true (handoff useful). I'll downgrade ready→partial when mismatches exist AND add failed-style entries? Hmm, failed entries drive "Could not add" UI. A modifier mismatch shown under "Could not add" would be wrong (it WAS added, wrongly).

Cleaner: keep cart.status logic as-is (ready/partial/failed based on added vs failed), add `cart["verification"]` block always (when a source order exists), and render a dedicated "Cart check" section in preview.js that is prominent: green "matches" / red-amber "differences to fix before paying" / grey "couldn't confirm". The handoff button stays (organizer can fix in the editable clone — that's exactly the action available), but the panel tells them what to fix. Also add verification warnings into cart.warnings? Warnings render as store-alert warning paragraphs already. I'll append a concise warning when mismatched/unverified so it's visible even without JS changes... but JS changes are needed anyway for the detailed panel.

Also idempotent-rebuild path: `existing.get("status")=="ready"` reuse — must carry verification forward (it's inside cart dict, so it does).

Also `_prebuild_failure` and `finish` should include verification? For failed builds with no order, verification = {"status":"unverified", reason...}? Better: only set verification when we attempted a read. For prebuild failures there's nothing to verify; omit or set unverified with reason "no cart was built". Keep it simple: set verification in finish() when order_id exists; else verification {"status":"unverified","reason":"no cart was built..."}? Hmm — for failed builds the UI shows error already; verification panel irrelevant. I'll set verification only when a source order was created (order_id not None), else None. Actually simpler and more predictable: always include the key; use "unverified" with reason when no read happened. Let me think about what the JS renders: if verification.status == matched → success note; mismatched → issue list; unverified → plain warning "couldn't confirm". For failed builds (no handoff), showing "couldn't confirm" is noise; the error is already shown. So: include verification only when order_id present. JS guards on its presence.

Edge: existing test `test_final_cart_readback_moves_a_missing_line_to_failed` expects failed code verification_failed and counts. Keep that exact behavior for lines absent from read-back. New semantic check runs after: for confirmed lines, compare modifiers/quantity; mismatches recorded in verification.mismatches; if any mismatch of kind modifiers/short_quantity and status was "ready", downgrade to "partial"? Let me decide: yes, downgrade ready→partial when verification finds wrong-content lines, because "ready" currently means "Your Kung Fu Tea cart is ready to review" which implies all good. Partial message "ready, with a few drinks left out" isn't quite right either for wrong modifiers... The JS headline could consider verification: if verification.status==mismatched → headline "The cart needs a look before you pay." That's the actionable moment. I'll add JS logic: headline priority — failed → could not be made; verification mismatched → "Check the cart before you pay — N difference(s)"; partial → left out; ready → ready to review.

For counts: keep as-is (added_rows/drinks reflect lines present). Mismatches don't change counts; they're detailed in verification. But missing-line case already moves to failed (counts updated). Good.

Also totals drift: verification compares expected vs actual subtotal; mismatch kind "totals" with detail. Don't change cart.totals (live values win).
